'''Brian J. Ford''' [[Fellow of the Linnean Society|HonFLS]] [[HonFRMS]] (born on May 13, 1939 in [[Corsham]], Wiltshire<ref>GRO Register of Births: JUN 1939 5a 88 CHIPPENHAM – Brian J. Ford</ref>) is an independent research biologist, author, and lecturer, who publishes on scientific issues for the general public. He has also been a television personality for more than 40 years. Ford is an international authority on the microscope.<ref name="B.J.Ford">{{cite web|title=Brian J Ford: Life through a microscope |url=https://analyticalscience.wiley.com/do/10.1002/micro.2378|website=[[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]]|accessdate=9 Oct 2017|date=27 January 2017|doi=<!-- none --> }}</ref> Throughout his career, Ford has been associated with many academic bodies. He was elected a Fellow of Cardiff University in 1986, was appointed Visiting Professor at the University of Leicester,<ref name="Scientist">{{cite web|title=Scientist, Author and Broadcaster to Support University's Developments in E-Learning|url=https://www.le.ac.uk/ebulletin-archive/ebulletin/news/press-releases/2000-2009/2005/11/nparticle-jb7-ndd-mgd.html|website=[[Leicester]]|accessdate=15 March 2013|location=Leicester, UK|language=English|date=10 February 2013}}</ref> and has been awarded Honorary Fellowship of the Royal Microscopical Society<ref name="Fellow">{{cite web|title=New Honorary Fellow Announced|url=https://www.rms.org.uk/study-read/news-listing-page/new-honorary-fellow-announced-brian-j-ford.html|website=[[Royal Microscopical Society]]|accessdate=16 March 2017|location=Leicester, UK|language=English|date=1 January 2017|archive-date=16 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316113403/http://www.rms.org.uk/study-read/news-listing-page/new-honorary-fellow-announced-brian-j-ford.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and of the Linnean Society of London.<ref name="Linnean">{{cite web|title=Congratulations to our newly-elected Fellows 'honoris causa'|url=https://www.linnean.org/news/2021/06/07/congratulations-to-our-newly-elected-fellows-honoris-causa|website=[[Linnean Society]]|accessdate=7 June 2021|location=Leicester, UK|language=English|date=10 January 2021}}</ref> In America, he was awarded the inaugural Köhler Medal<ref name="Kohler">{{cite web|title=Brian J Ford wins inaugural Köhler medal in America|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358286170|website=[[ResearchGate]]|accessdate=11 November 2020|location=New York, US|language=English|date=17 August 2020}}</ref> and was recently recipient of the Ernst Abbe medal awarded by the New York Microscopical Society.<ref name="Abbe">{{cite web|title=Brian J. Ford Receives the New York Microscopical Society Ernst Abbe Award|url=https://www.spectroscopyonline.com/view/brian-j-ford-receives-the-new-york-microscopical-society-ernst-abbe-award|website=[[Ernst Abbe]]|accessdate=11 November 2020|location=New York, US|language=English|date=17 August 2020}}</ref> In 2004 he was awarded a personal fellowship from NESTA,<ref name="NESTA">{{cite web|title=The NESTA Reports by Brian J Ford|url=https://issuu.com/sciencepublications/docs/nesta-reports|website=[[Nesta (charity)]]|accessdate=18 November 2021|location=Illinois, US|language=English|date=7 August 2021}}</ref> the National Endowment for Science, Technology and the Arts. During those three years he delivered 150 lectures in scores of countries, meeting 10,000 people in over 350 universities around the world.

== Education ==
Ford attended the [[The King's School, Peterborough|King's School]], [[Peterborough]], and then [[Cardiff University]] to study [[botany]] and [[zoology]] between 1959 and 1961, leaving before graduating to set up his own multi-disciplinary laboratory.<ref name="HonFRMS">{{cite web|title=Prof Brian J Ford announced as RMS Honorary Fellow|url=http://www.rms.org.uk/study-read/news-listing-page/new-honorary-fellow-announced-brian-j-ford.html|website=[[Royal Microscopical Society]]|accessdate=15 March 2017|location=Oxford, UK|language=English|date=27 February 2017}}</ref>

===Learned Societies===
*Fellow of the [[Linnean Society]] - serving as a member of their council as their Zoological Secretary and is their honorary surveyor of scientific instruments<ref name="HonFRMS"/>
*Fellow of the [[Institute of Biology]] - a former member of their council and chairman of their history network<ref name="HonFRMS"/> (He also edited: ''Institute of Biology: The First Fifty Years'' which is devoted to the history of this Institute.<ref>''Institute of Biology: The First Fifty Years'', Institute of Biology, {{ISBN|0-900490-37-3}}</ref>)
*Life fellow of [[Cambridge Philosophical Society]]
*Fellowship by the [[NESTA|National Endowment for Science, Technology and Art]] in 2004
*[[HonFRMS|Honorary Fellow of the Royal Microscopical Society]] - appointed in February 2017, having been elected as an ordinary fellow in 1962<ref name="HonFRMS"/>

=== Other positions ===
He was the first British President of the European Union of Science Journalists' Associations,{{Citation needed|date=October 2007}} founding Chairman of the Science and Technology Authors Committee at the [[Society of Authors]], {{Citation needed|date=October 2007}} and the president of the Cambridge Society for the Application of Research (CSAR) of Cambridge University.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.csar.org.uk/|title=Society for the Application of Research.}}</ref> Ford has been a member of [[Mensa International|Mensa]] and was a director of British Mensa from 1993–1997, resigning a few months after being elected for a second term.<ref>"Mensa Elections", p.4, ''Mensa Magazine'' October 1993</ref><ref>"Musical Chairs", p.4, ''Mensa Magazine'' March 1998</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Microscopical Society in 1962.

== Aquatic dinosaur hypothesis ==
In the April 2012 issue of ''[[Laboratory News]]'', Ford put forward the idea that all large dinosaurs were aquatic, arguing that they were too large and heavy to be land animals.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.labnews.co.uk/features/prehistoric-revolution-2/|date=3 April 2012|title=A prehistoric revolution|last=Ford|first=Brian J|magazine=Laboratory News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140921072203/http://www.labnews.co.uk/features/prehistoric-revolution-2/|archive-date=21 September 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2018, ''Too Big To Walk: The New Science of Dinosaurs,'' a book authored by Ford and published by William Collins (an imprint of [[HarperCollins]]), was released expounding on this hypothesis.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Naish |first=Darren |date=2025-09-02 |title=The response to and rejection of Brian Ford's Too Big to Walk, a 21 st century effort to reinstate the aquatic dinosaur hypothesis |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/08912963.2024.2421268 |journal=Historical Biology |language=en |volume=37 |issue=9 |pages=2147–2156 |doi=10.1080/08912963.2024.2421268 |issn=0891-2963|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Although evidence has been presented for some dinosaurs like [[Spinosauridae|spinosaurids]] being partially aquatic, reaction to Ford's theory that the majority of dinosaurs being largely aquatic have been highly, if not universally negative, with other experts in the fields of paleontology and paleobiology having continuously disproven or refuted Ford's claims,<ref name=":0" /> with some suggesting Ford's hypotheses could be relegated as fringe theories. Several paleontologists, such as Darren Naish, have directly countered Ford in his arguments using documented evidence of dinosaurs being terrestrial to back their rebuttals to his work.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://inquisitivebiologist.com/2018/06/25/book-review-too-big-to-walk-the-new-science-of-dinosaurs/ | title=Book review – Too Big to Walk: The New Science of Dinosaurs | date=25 June 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | first=Darren | last=Naish | title=A Vast Quantity of Evidence Confirms That Non-Bird Dinosaurs Were Not Aquatic | url=https://darrennaish.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/corrections-to-brian-j-ford-dinosaur-claims-may-2018.pdf | access-date=2025-09-07}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://pteroformer.blogspot.com/2018/05/ford-vs-naish-too-big-to-walk.html | title=Pteroformer: Ford vs. Naish - 'Too Big to Walk' | date=16 May 2018 }}</ref>
